summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose about 50% to Rs 318 crore; EBITDA margin 10% and PAT margin 6%, with polymer flame-retardant capacity not yet commercial.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of Rs 318 crore, up about 50% from Rs 212 crore in FY25, with EBITDA margin up from 9% to 10% and PAT margin up from 5% to 6%. Sales volume rose from about 32,000-33,000 MT to 46,000 MT, which management said includes about 4,400 MT from in-house manufacturing. Management attributed H2 growth to raw-material price increases from January, volume sales, and sourcing ahead of demand, and said H2 gross margin was squeezed by those input costs. The halogen-free polymer flame-retardant plant (400 MT/month) is still in teething trouble and is expected to be commercial in the next three to six months. Many answers were forward-looking or deferred, and the call was largely Q&A from individual investors.

segments.name: Food and feed additives (manufacturing)
segments.commentary: Running at about 95% utilisation; a food additive line was recently added and is almost fully used. Management cited ~30% gross margin for manufacturing overall.

segments.name: Polymer additives (halogen-free flame retardants)
segments.commentary: Plant capacity of 400 MT per month is not yet at full run-rate due to teething issues; trials with five customers and NDAs signed with two. Management guided to ~40% margins and an average price of about Rs 250/kg-equivalent, implying ~Rs 100 crore revenue at full utilisation.

segments.name: Petrochemical trading (base oils, TG urea)
segments.commentary: Gross margin ~21%. Management said petrochemicals contributed most to FY26 turnover growth; melamine and phenol are not traded.

guidance_outlook: Polymer additive plant expected to be fully running in three to six months; contribution expected in FY27.
Plan to scale total capacity to 18,000 MT in phases over 12 to 18 months, with about Rs 20 crore capex across FY27 and FY28, funded by bank credit lines and IPO proceeds.
Target to lift manufacturing share of revenue from 23% to 50% in two to three years.
Working capital cycle reduction targeted, via invoice discounting for buyers and buyer's/supplier's credit with suppliers.
Management declined to give FY27 growth numbers, saying momentum would be maintained but this was forward-looking.
Three patents to be filed within six months.
capex_capacity: Current installed capacity stated as 6,600 MT; manufacturing was 2,800 MT last year and 4,600 MT this year (figures given in different answers).
Food and feed lines running at ~95%; overall capacity utilisation ~70% after polymer additive addition.
Polymer additive plant: 400 MT/month (also cited as 450 MT/month), currently 600 MT base, to be expanded to 18,000 MT in phases over 12 to 18 months.
Capex of ~Rs 20 crore for polymer additives and compounding facility in FY27 and FY28, on a 9.6-acre land parcel (also cited as 10 acres).
Omega-3 and Vitamin D2 products remain in R&D, at pilot/industrial trial stage; no commercial timeline given.
demand_pricing: Raw material prices rose sharply from January to February; some products roughly doubled in the last six months, per management.
Geopolitical disruption has cut overseas-sourced material supply in India, which management said hurt its three-month import-trading stock but created demand for domestic manufactured alternatives.
Halogen-free flame retardants: management says no direct Indian competitor, competing in a 'blue ocean', and said it does not need to offer discounts; interest also received from foreign buyers.
Government orders are typically one-year contracts (six-month to one-year cited); private customers give quantity-based or three-month contracts.
End markets for flame retardants: cable and wire and electrical/electronics equipment first, with EV batteries targeted later.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue almost double in H2 FY26 versus H1, and why did margins decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a mix of higher prices and volume, driven by sourcing ahead of demand from December and raw material price increases from January/February, which compressed margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the utilisation by segment and the organic headroom before the next capex cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Food and feed run at ~95%; polymer plant is not yet live. Rs 20 crore capex planned for FY27-28 to reach 18,000 MT over 12 to 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: How will the planned capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Through a mix of bank credit lines for capex and remaining IPO proceeds; no split given.

qa_highlights.question: When will the halogen-free flame retardant contribute, and what is the run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant can be operational within about three months; customer testing takes three to six months; full utilisation expected within about six months. Management said it would contribute in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle is 110 days and management is working to reduce it through invoice discounting for buyers and buyer's and supplier's credit; some suppliers still require full advance payment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Omega-3 and Vitamin D2 status?
qa_highlights.answer: In R&D, at final pilot/industrial trial stage; no commercial date can be given.

qa_highlights.question: Could the company's peak revenue from the 400 MT polymer plant be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: At an average price of about Rs 250 per kg, 400 MT per month equates to roughly Rs 100 crore of annual turnover at full utilisation, per management.

risks_watch: Polymer additive ramp-up delays: teething issues and customer qualification could push revenue beyond FY27 H1.
Raw material cost volatility and supply disruption from geopolitical factors; reliance on overseas suppliers and three-month stock buffer.
Working capital cycle at 110 days, with receivable days rising; cash flow pressure from advance-payment suppliers.
Government contracts are a large share of the Rs 55 crore order book (Rs 42 crore), with renewal risk.
Competition risk if a rival replicates the halogen-free product; three patents yet to be filed.
Management did not answer on a plant visit and offered no FY27 growth guidance; disclosure gaps in some figures (volume, capacity, land area) across answers.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the polymer additive opportunity and long-term growth, but evasive on forward numbers, with repeated 'forward-looking' caveats. Several answers were unclear or deferred to later follow-up, and figures given varied across answers.
